title: No validation of special IPv6 addresses in routing messages
description:
File: rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs
Lines: 376-381, 443-449, 520-523

The parsers accept any 16-byte value as IPv6 addresses without validating against special addresses that are invalid for routing:
- `::` (unspecified) 
- `::1` (loopback)
- `ff00::/8` (multicast)
- `fe80::/10` link-local (may be intentionally valid)

Bad outcome: Attacker sends RREQ with `destination=::` or RERR with `unreachable=ff02::1`, potentially causing route table corruption or unexpected behavior when the stack tries to route to/from these addresses.

This might be intentional if validation happens at a higher layer, but for defense in depth the codec layer should reject obviously invalid addresses.
